title: Live-cell imaging-based microglia phagocytosis assay using AI on Olympus ScanR system
author: Zähringer, Vinnakota, et al.

steps.title: Prepare pHrodo BioParticles
steps.instruction: Dissolve the lyophilized pHrodo BioParticles Conjugates for phagocytosis according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Store pHrodo BioParticles
steps.instruction: Aliquot the dissolved pHrodo BioParticles and keep them at 4 °C; use within a maximum of 3 months.

steps.title: Prepare FluoroBrite medium
steps.instruction: Make FluoroBrite Medium and supplement it with 10 % fetal calf serum (FCS) and any other required supplements, ensuring the medium contains no fluorescent substances.

steps.title: Plate microglia cells
steps.instruction: One or two days before imaging, seed 10 000 cells per well into a 96‑well plate with a glass bottom; start any required pretreatment of the cells.

substeps.instruction: If cells do not adhere well, pre‑coat the plate according to a pilot test.

steps.title: Pre‑warm reagents
steps.instruction: On the day of live‑cell imaging, warm all reagents (medium, pHrodo particles, etc.) to 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare computational resources
steps.instruction: Ensure a workstation with at least an Intel Xeon W‑2255 CPU (3.70 GHz), 64 GB RAM, 64‑bit OS, NVIDIA Quadro RTX 4000 GPU, and access to the institutional network server where the imaging dataset is stored.

steps.title: Download and import neural network
steps.instruction: Download the AIstain U‑Net neural network from the provided Mendeley Data link and import it via ScanR → AI → Manage Neural Networks → Import.

steps.title: Create new assay with virtual channel
steps.instruction: In ScanR, choose Analysis → New Assay, then go to Assay Settings → Virtual Channels, select “neural network processing” as the module, press New, and choose the imported AIstain network.

steps.title: Configure image processing
steps.instruction: In the Image Processing tab, enable “Background correction for pHrodo”.

steps.title: Define main object and threshold
steps.instruction: In the Main Object tab, select “cytoplasm probability” as the channel, choose “Intensity”, press Adjust, enable “Watershed on”, and set the detection threshold.

substeps.instruction: Use the Auto threshold function, then reduce the automatically set value by 1–5 % manually.
Verify the threshold on several images via the right‑hand list; adjust if necessary.

steps.title: Select analysis parameters
steps.instruction: In the Parameters tab, choose Auto to generate a full list, confirming that “Time”, “Total Intensity pHrodo”, and “Mean Intensity pHrodo” appear for the main object.

steps.title: Save assay definition
steps.instruction: Close the settings window and save the assay via Analysis → Save Assay.

steps.title: Test assay on a well
steps.instruction: Select a single well in the lower‑left well selector and press Run to verify cell detection.

substeps.instruction: If images appear gray or no cells are detected, consult troubleshooting.
Overlay the “objects probability” channel to visualise the neural‑network segmentation.

steps.title: Set gating parameters (Area, Circularity)
steps.instruction: In the first plot, set X = Area and Y = Circularity factor, then draw a gate around the cell population as illustrated in the protocol.

steps.title: Create “Cells” gate
steps.instruction: Open Analysis → Assay Gating, press New, and define a gate named “Cells” using the Area vs. Circularity parameters.

steps.title: Apply cell gate to second plot
steps.instruction: In the second plot, right‑click, set gate to “Cells”, so only gated cells are displayed.

steps.title: Define time‑point gate
steps.instruction: In the second plot, set X = Time and Y = Total intensity pHrodo, then draw a rectangular gate around the desired time point (e.g., label it R02).

steps.title: Create “Timepoint” gate
steps.instruction: Open Analysis → Assay Gating, press New, and create a gate named “Timepoint” using the Time vs. Total intensity parameters.

steps.title: Save assay before batch run
steps.instruction: Save the assay again (Analysis → Save Assay). You may pause here and resume later.

steps.title: Run batch analysis
steps.instruction: Open Analysis → Batch run, select the imaging scan, the saved assay, and a storage directory (rename output file if desired), then press New and Run.

substeps.instruction: The batch will run in the background; expected runtime is ~4 h for 8 wells × 25 images × 14 time points on the specified hardware.

steps.title: Export numeric data
steps.instruction: When batch analysis finishes, open the results (Analysis → Open), select the desired well, set the “Timepoint” gate at the required time, then go to Analysis → Assay Gating → Well results, choose the gate and parameter(s), and click Export to generate a .txt file.

substeps.instruction: For single‑cell data, use Analysis → Export.

steps.title: Adjust gating for other cell types
steps.instruction: If analyzing larger or more ramified cells, increase the Area range and/or Circularity factor of the “Cells” gate accordingly; visualize the gate via right‑click → Show Gallery.

steps.title: Plate cells and add beads (adaptation)
steps.instruction: For any phagocytic cell type, plate 10 000 cells per well in a 96‑well glass‑bottom plate and add the same amount of pHrodo BioParticles beads as used for microglia; determine incubation time on the microscope in a pilot study.

steps.title: Select X and Y parameters (optional)
steps.instruction: In the assay settings (step 35), choose the desired X and Y parameters from the drop‑down menus to enable coordinate‑based plotting.

steps.title: Downstream single‑cell analysis in R
steps.instruction: Use the provided R script to read the exported .txt/.xlsx file and generate an intensity heat‑map of Total Intensity pHrodo across X‑Y coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Install ggplot2, readxl, and ggpubr packages.
Adjust column names in the script if they differ.
